newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN DOLLAR DEPOSITS QUIETLY STEADY IN LATE TRADE.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN DOLLAR DEPOSITS QUIETLY STEADY IN LATE TRADE.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were quietly steady in moderate trade on Wednesday with most traders sidelined ahead of tonight's release of the U.S. July retail sales and producer price index (PPI) data, dealers said.
Retail sales for July were forecast to show an increase of 0.7 percent compared with a 0.5 percent gain reported in June.
The July producer price index is expected to show a gain of 0.1 percent against June's 0.1 percent decline.
"Rates were quietly steady in the morning except for some light activity at the short and long end of the market," a local dealer said.
"Some traders were waiting for fresh clues to market direction from tonight's release of the retail sales and producer price index," he said.
"The numbers have been built into the market and most people have squared or are squaring their positions for the day, so I don't think there will be much impact here," he added.
In day-to-day rates, Wednesday/Thursday was unchanged from Tuesday's 5-11/16 5-9/16 percent and Thursday/Friday unchanged at 5-5/8 5-1/2 percent.
Week-fixed rose 1/16 percentage point to 5-5/8 5-1/2 percent.
Among longer dates, one-month was unchanged at 5-5/8 5-1/2 percent, three-months unchanged at 5-3/4 5-5/8 and nine-months unchanged at 6 5-7/8 percent.
